## Author’s Preface to the Reader.

1. Since we now, through grace and the light of Christ, find that fallen humanity has so completely turned away from the essence of God <note>original: "Wesen Gottes"; in this mystical context, "essence" refers to the actual substance or presence of God within the soul, rather than just an idea about God.</note> toward earthly, pictorial things or imaginations <note>original: "Imaginationen"; the author uses this to mean mental constructs or fantasies that distract from spiritual reality.</note> with their earthly desires and reason—whereby they have become so blind to the working of God <note>original: "Wirckung Gottes"; the active, transformative power of God within a person.</note> that it is as if they had no heavenly, essential God—we have therefore been caused or moved by the essential God to testify a little concerning the inward, essential working of God (which God works through His Spirit, in a teaching manner, in obedient humanity). In contrast, we aim to reveal and make known the false working of the earthly nature, also in a teaching manner, within the heart of humanity. It is our hope that the Lord will grant His blessing and prosperity to this end, so that blind eyes might be opened a little to perceive the workings of God in the soul, and to distinguish them from the false workings of earthly reason <note>original: "irdische Vernunfft"; for mystical writers like Hiel, "earthly reason" is the limited human intellect that tries to understand God through logic rather than through direct spiritual experience.</note>.

2. For as long as humanity does not commit its inward soul out of earthly reason and into the working of God, the senses and thoughts run through earthly reason toward the elemental, pictorial imagi-

->With what diligence the internal speech is to be observed.<-

This is so that in this dangerous time, she <note>The soul (die Seele) is grammatically feminine in German and is often personified as a female figure in mystical literature.</note> should allow her blind eyes and deafened ears to be opened by the resonance and voice of the spiritual and essential Christ of God, so that she may see, hear, and perceive or feel who speaks within her and who holds dominion over her; whether it be the holy essence <term>Wesen: The true, inner substance or "being" of God as opposed to mere external forms.</term> of God, or earthly reason <term>Vernunfft: In this mystical context, "reason" often refers to the limited, human intellect that relies on itself rather than divine illumination.</term> through the essence of the devil.

Foundations of Christ’s and the Devil’s School. Chapter XV.

### The Fifteenth Chapter.

->The School of Christ and of the Devil: Both as the<-
->greatest wonder in man.<-

1. If anyone now wishes to become a partaker of the gifts of God—which He now, in this final portion of time, allows to appear out of His hidden heaven through His long-suffering grace—he must first and above all else take heed of the teaching of the gentle spirit of Christ, and be subject to it in all obedience.

2. And this teaching must be learned in the obedient Divine School of Christ. That is, in the holy denial of oneself.

3. And whoever will not obediently deny himself cannot come into the School of Christ to be taught by the gentle spirit of Christ; such a person must remain in hardened <note>original: *ver-sten*, likely *verstockten* (hardened) or *versteinerten* (petrified)</note> heathendom to his own damnation, under the teaching of the cruel, unmerciful property <term>Eigenschafft: a technical term in this context referring to the self-centered "own-ness" or the inherent quality of the fallen human ego</term> of the flesh, in evil, surging unrest. And there the Devil—the adversary <note>original: *Widerwesen*, meaning a counter-being or oppositional nature</note> of God—is the schoolmaster. He teaches the soul nothing but hate, envy, vengefulness, torment, and unrest, according to the kind and nature of the Devil; through which all divine virtue is suppressed and overwhelmed.

<margin><image-desc>manicule pointing right</image-desc></margin>

1. In this, we must praise, thank, and laud God’s grace above all others. For the greater the gift—to overcome the evil, godless nature—the greater and more profound our gratitude should be.

# Fundamental Warning against Offense Ch. XXXVI

[...fruits] they should take from the divided rational opinions and not let this unified <term>unified [original: *einwesige*] — a term describing a state where the soul is no longer split by various worldly distractions but is one with God’s essence.</term> Light of Life pass by, but rather be united with the same into one essence and spirit, so that they may not have cause to complain regarding the neglected time, and that they paid no heed to the blessed time and work of the **LORD**, and have blinded themselves so completely in their earthly lusts that they do not think once upon the work of the **LORD** (just as happened formerly among the heedless godless), as the Prophet <margin>Isa. <note>original: "Es." refers to Esaias (Isaiah 5:11-12).</note></margin> says, that they sit in wine until the night and follow their godless merrymaking with all kinds of games.

2. ### Fundamental Word on Death and Life/etc. Ch. XLIV. ###

6. Therefore, life witnesses of life, how perfect it is in all living heavenly riches: so that it lacks nothing. Indeed, the wealth within life is so abundant that one cannot estimate or describe it.

### Fundamental Word on Death and Life / etc. Ch. XLVI ###

10. O wretched humanity / you who are seized by damnable death; how greatly and heavily you have prepared death for yourself. For God did not want / that death should have power over humanity. Therefore he works zealously through his Spirit; to strip death of its power. As he says: *O Death! I was your death and sting.* <note>original: "O Tod ! Ich war dein Tod und Stachel." A reference to Hosea 13:14, often interpreted in this period as Christ's victory over the grave.</note> Hos. 13:14.

11. And to strip this death of its power / the provident <term>provident: *vorsichtige*, here meaning "foreseeing" or "providential" rather than "cautious."</term> wisdom of God / has used various means / and has first shown himself / in his righteousness against the death of sins / to humanity; which introduced death through sin; and placed that same humanity out of the life into the death / which it had prepared for itself.

12. And while they stood in the death of sins / God sent his prophecy of Enos <note>Enos, the grandson of Adam. In mystical theology, Enos represents the first stage of the "re-awakening" of humanity, as Genesis 4:26 states that in his time men began to call upon the name of the Lord.</note>; which was partly human; to humanity who stood in the death of sins. And thereby the righteous Godhead came to the aid of humanity / which was weak against God’s righteousness / because it could not endure the heavenly righteousness of God. And he had it proclaimed to them / that they should take back their desire <note>original: *Lust*, referring to the orientation of the will or the soul's longing.</note> / which they had surrendered to the death of sins / and should bring that same desire to the living God in life. And to this prophecy he added his Law / with punishment and the killing of sins / in order to bring humanity back against the death / which it had taken in.

### The Fifty-Sixth Chapter.

->Two Kinds of Rewards: The Example of Ahab.<-

<margin>1.</margin>
Look: The reason we have described these birth-pangs <note>original: "Wehen," referring to the "Woes" previously discussed, but also carrying the biblical connotation of labor pains or intense suffering before a transition.</note> here in part is so that humanity may be shown and recognize that as soon as it receives or consents to sin with its lust, it becomes subject to these birth-pangs and must expect them every moment through God’s justice.

2. On the other hand, humanity that stands in obedience to God and has no desire to sin is expecting all of God’s joys with every blessing and benediction that God has in His heaven. For the Godhead has no good for Himself alone; rather, His good is shared in common with all His saints.

3. Pay close attention! These are unequal rewards for the soul. Therefore, humanity may well take care under whom they perform their service to receive a reward.

4. However, humanity is so blinded in its pride that it pays no heed to the warning of the birth-pangs to which it is subject. Nevertheless, it allows itself to think it wants to justify all its affairs with God’s testimony; therefore, they also ask all their prophets for advice. ## The Sixty-Eighth Chapter.
->The true Christ in us is our salvation.<-

1. Oh, my dear simple hearts, you who strive for your salvation with simplicity: do not believe in such a delusory Christ who is outside of your heart and soul. Instead, take your refuge in a Christ who is born within your soul out of a humbled, obedient, and heavenly spirit, and who goes before your soul in all obedient, godly virtue; both in death (according to the flesh) and in life (according to the spirit), until reaching eternal blessedness. By this He proves that He is Jesus—that is, the Savior <note>original: "Seeligmacher"; literally "one who makes blessed" or "bringer of salvation"</note>.

2. And such a Christ has now appeared in a unified life <note>original: "einwesigen Leben"; a mystical term referring to a life where the human essence is united with the divine essence</note> to us who are small and poor in spirit in this final portion of time. We proclaim this same Christ to the lovers of truth. ### Conclusion.

That this testimony <note>original: "Zeugnuß." The author refers to the book itself as a spiritual witness or testimony.</note> is witnessed from the Spirit of Christ for the direction of a godly Christian life / which proves its power in the heart of the obedient person / to drive out all earthly spirits. Those who judge this testimony will wound no one but themselves. That one should judge oneself and one's own evil heart. The author's intention is not to write against anyone's religion. Explains only the divine Christian foundation in the heart of humanity. The cunning of the earthly spirit to deceive man. Accepting the false light of reason <term>Vernunfft-Liecht: In mystical thought, this refers to human intellect or logic that attempts to understand God without the aid of divine revelation or spiritual experience.</term> in place of the Spirit of God. Paying attention to the essential Church of Christ <note>original: "wesentliche Kirch Christi." This refers to the invisible, spiritual reality of the Church as the body of Christ, rather than any specific denomination or building.</note> / so that the soul is redeemed from sin. The blindness of the earthly man / arising from the light of reason / to charm himself and others with idle chatter. What should those do who doubt this testimony / whether it be from God? To obey the testimony / either spiritually in divine obedience / or in human servitude; beneath the letter <note>A reference to "the letter" of the law or scripture without the "spirit."</note> man has lost the knowledge of God and himself / and lives only by the imagination of his reason. Neither God nor the Devil can move a hardened man. But misery and tribulation follow / when things do not go according to his own mind. Exhortation to depart from the great delusion <note>original: "Verblendung." A state of being spiritually blinded or deceived by worldly things.</note>. From whence this fundamental piece <note>original: "Grund-Stuck." This likely refers to the treatise or specific book this index describes.</note> takes its name?
